title: Longest Substring Without Repeats

concept.title: Remember where each letter was last seen
body: Keep a window `[start, i]` that contains no repeated letter. When the next letter `ch` already occurs inside the window, the window must start right after the previous occurrence of `ch`. A table `last` that stores the last position of every letter gives this in O(1).
The test `last[ch] >= start` ignores occurrences that are already outside the window. The start never moves backwards, so one pass is enough.

statement: Given a word, find the length of its longest block of consecutive letters in which all letters are different.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: The longest such block is abc, length 3.

hints: Keep a window with all letters different.
Remember the last position of every letter.
When a letter repeats inside the window, move the start to just after its previous position.

explanation: The window start jumps to just after the previous occurrence of a repeated letter, so the window never contains duplicates.
solution.complexity: Time O(n), space O(1) (a table with one entry per letter).
